svg.title: A single stacked bar for the monthly cost of one manual step. The solid lower block is the visible labour cost of 11,340 rupees, which is where most estimates stop. Stacked above it are three blocks nobody counts: 2,700 rupees of errors and rework, 3,780 rupees of context switching, and 2,660 rupees of cover when the one person who owns the process is away. The full stack is 20,480 rupees a month, so the visible half is 55 per cent of the real figure. A separate note explains that opportunity cost replaces the labour block rather than stacking on top of it.

g.text: WHERE THE COST OF ONE MANUAL STEP ACTUALLY SITS
Enquiry intake — 252 a month, 6 minutes each, at a loaded rate of ₹450 an hour
THE REAL FIGURE
₹20,480 a month
the part people see
MOST ESTIMATES
STOP AT THIS LINE
6 min × 252 × ₹450 an hour
Three inputs, nothing else
Minutes per run. Runs per month.
Loaded rate. Every figure on this
diagram comes out of those three.
Cover when the owner is away — ₹2,660
28 days off a year, covered at ₹700 an hour, less the ₹450 it replaces
One person owns this. That is a standing cost, not a vague risk.
Context switching — ₹3,780
2 minutes of re-orientation per pickup × 252 = 8.4 hours a month
The softest number here. Measure it on your own desk, or halve it.
Errors and rework — ₹2,700
8% of 252 go wrong × 18 minutes to notice, chase and fix = 6 hours
Fixing one costs three times what entering it did.
The visible labour — ₹11,340
6 min × 252 a month = 25.2 hours, at the loaded rate of ₹450
Salary alone would have said ₹8,400. Salary is not the cost.
Opportunity cost is not a fifth block
What this person would otherwise earn replaces the labour block —
it never stacks on top. Count the larger, and say which one you used.
